summary: Burst of OAuth token refreshes and service-account API calls after clicking external feedback link
description: Issue summary: Multiple Redwood employees reported suspicious account activity after interacting with a third-party 'Feedback Survey' link in an external vendor email. Detection systems flagged abnormal OAuth token refresh patterns and service-account enumeration attempts originating from IPs not previously seen in our org. This ticket is to track triage, containment, and investigation.
impact: Potential exposure of session tokens for ~8 employees who clicked the link. No confirmed data exfiltration yet. Temporary disruption to a small number of CI jobs that rely on short-lived service tokens.
detection: Automated anomaly alert from identity-monitoring: spike in /oauth/token POSTs from user agents matching common browsers but with atypical TLS SNI. Concurrently, audit log shows increased calls to IAM ListServiceAccounts from a subset of affected sessions.
timeline:
2026-03-12 08:21 UTC - First alert from identity-monitoring.
2026-03-12 08:30 UTC - SOC team initial review; identified 7 unique employee sessions.
2026-03-12 09:05 UTC - Support contacted affected users to revoke active sessions.
2026-03-12 10:12 UTC - Blocked outbound requests to suspected vendor domains via egress ACLs.
2026-03-12 12:40 UTC - Rotated OAuth client secrets for a small internal integration.
2026-03-13 15:00 UTC - Forensics on logs shows refresh pattern correlating with clicks on embedded marketing link.
2026-03-14 11:15 UTC - SRE and security running targeted hunts for lateral token use.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Open employee mailbox containing the vendor marketing email. 2) Click embedded 'Feedback Survey' link (do not actually perform on a real account; use isolated test account). 3) Observe redirect chain (likely includes 3rd-party tracking domain). 4) Monitor oauth/token POST requests from the browser session and audit logs for any service-account calls triggered after token refresh.
logs:
Identity logs (oauth/token POSTs) available in SIEM: indices redwood-identity-2026-03-12. Example entries: 
- 2026-03-12T08:24:10Z user=a.khan ip=18.205.33.12 ua=Mozilla/5.0 refresh=true sni=survey-track.example.net
- 2026-03-12T08:24:15Z service=ci-runner action=ListServiceAccounts token_subject=a.khan ip=34.201.11.4
Link to raw slices: https://siem.internal.redwood/runs/abc123 (access restricted)
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis: The vendor email contained an embedded redirect that performed an OAuth token refresh via a hidden iframe or redirect with a CSRF-like pattern, capturing refresh tokens or prompting a silent token exchange. Evidence shows clustering around the survey domain and a small subset of IPs associated with ad/tracking networks. No clear signs of long-lived API keys being exfiltrated.
Partial findings:
- Affected sessions all used single-sign-on (IdP) and had previously active device sessions.
- Refresh bursts resumed for ~30s after initial click and then subsided for most users after session revocation.
- One CI job did attempt IAM ListServiceAccounts; the token used was short-lived and scoped to the user's session.
Open questions:
- Did the redirect chain include an authorization_code leak to a 3rd-party callback?
- Were any refresh tokens persisted server-side by the vendor?
actions_taken:
- Immediate: Support contacted impacted employees and forced web session sign-outs for 8 users.
- Containment: Blocked egress to identified tracking domains in prod us-east at 09:05 UTC.
- Credentials: Rotated two OAuth client secrets used by an internal integration that showed anomalous requests.
- Detection: Created a SIEM rule to alert on refresh bursts of >5 token refreshes/min per user and on ListServiceAccounts following a refresh within 60s.
- Notification: Security sent an org-wide advisory to avoid interacting with the vendor email until further notice.
next_steps:
- Forensics: Extract full redirect chains from web proxy logs for all affected users (owner: Marco Rivera, due 2026-03-15).
- Hunt: Expand search for similar patterns across eu-west and ap-south logs (owner: SRE team).
- Vendor outreach: Security to request details from vendor on the survey redirect implementation (owner: Priya Desai).
- Post-incident: Draft email template for future similar events and update phishing-runbook with this threat pattern.
